free_tier.stated: USD 100 in credits on signup; the Linux box includes 10 GiB of storage free to use; no recurring no-cost allowance is published, and all vCPU, memory, emulator and device time is billed per second after credits
free_tier.notes: The signup credit is a one-time grant, not a recurring monthly allowance. The 10 GiB free storage applies to the Linux box only. Rates: Linux vCPU USD 0.054 per hour, memory USD 0.0144 per GiB-hour, both billed per second but shown hourly; Android emulator medium 4-core/8GB at USD 0.009 flat under 30 s then USD 0.0003 per second, large 8-core/16GB at USD 0.015 flat under 30 s then USD 0.0005 per second; physical device 8-core/8GB/128GB at USD 0.024 flat under 30 s then USD 0.0008 per second, with a 10-minute minimum charge.

per_object_cap.stated: 10 GiB of storage is free to use on a Linux box; no per-file or per-object cap is published on the pricing page

retention.stated: not stated: the pricing page publishes rates and a free storage allowance but says nothing about how long a box or its files survive

egress.terms: not published: the pricing page lists no egress allowance and no per-GB or per-TB price for traffic out of a box

interface_detail: A single SDK and API drive four environment types — Android mobile, Linux-Chrome browser, Linux-XFCE desktop and Linux-Ubuntu sandbox; the CLI and MCP integrations drive the same environments, and natural-language actions are a documented SDK feature.
tooling: gbox-sdk for TypeScript and Python, the REST API with a per-account API key, and the GBOX Android MCP / CLI integrations.
chaining: One account and key create mobile, browser, desktop and sandbox boxes, so an agent can move from a cheap sandbox to a real physical Android device under the same meter; the USD 100 signup credits buy a finite amount of billed seconds before per-second rates apply.

limits.value: USD 100 in signup credits, one-time; thereafter Linux vCPU USD 0.054 per hour and memory USD 0.0144 per GiB-hour, billed per second
10 GiB of Linux box storage free to use

limits_note: Android emulator has a 30-second minimum charge and physical devices a 10-minute minimum charge; physical-device availability is limited and the feature is beta. No request-rate ceiling is published on the pricing page.
binding_note: The one-time USD 100 credit is the first thing to run out: all four environment types draw from it at per-second rates with no recurring no-cost allowance published, while the 10 GiB storage allowance applies only to the Linux box.

identity_cost.detail: The API-key guide says to go to gbox.ai, log in to an account, then create and copy a key in the API Keys section; the privacy policy says registration asks the user to sign up using a GitHub account and receives the user's name, email address and profile photo from GitHub. A card is mentioned only as a payment method the user may add, so it is not established that a card is required for the signup credit. No phone or ID document is stated.

reliability_note: Physical-device boxes are a beta feature with limited availability and possible instability; emulator time carries a 30-second minimum charge and physical-device time a 10-minute minimum charge.
confidence_note: The rate card, the free 10 GiB storage and the USD 100 signup credit are quoted from GBOX's own pricing page read 2026-11-24; the GitHub signup gate is quoted from GBOX's own privacy page; the API-key gate and the four environment types are quoted from GBOX's own docs.
